monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month, with faster paces and more time in Zones 3–4, but at the cost of reduced volume and lower aerobic efficiency compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your cadence increased by 6 spm while vertical oscillation rose slightly (7.6 → 8.4 cm), suggesting a trade-off between turnover and form economy — especially evident in your fastest recent run (6:33 min/km, 162 spm, 8.4 cm VO).

goal_tracker.message: You need 19.3 more km across 4 remaining sessions — averaging 4.8 km per session — to match last month’s volume. Given your current pace trend (faster runs), consider prioritizing duration over speed in at least two of those sessions to support aerobic base.

insights.title: Efficiency improved despite higher intensity
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency rose from 13.42 to 13.95 — likely driven by increased cadence (146 → 152 spm) and improved stride coordination during faster efforts, as seen in your 3.0 km run (91.13 m stride, 274 ms ground contact, 8.4 cm VO).

insights.title: Zone 3–4 time doubled while Zone 1–2 dropped sharply
insights.body: Time in Z3+Z4 increased from 22% (last month) to 46% (this month), while Z1+Z2 fell from 79% to 51%. This reflects a clear shift toward threshold and tempo work — beneficial for race pace development, but risks under-recovery without adequate Z1/Z2 balance.

insights.title: Cadence-stride trade-off emerging at speed
insights.body: Your fastest run (6:33 min/km) had highest cadence (162 spm) and longest stride (91.13 m), yet vertical oscillation increased to 8.4 cm (vs. 7.6–7.7 cm in slower long/easy runs) and ground contact dropped to 274 ms — indicating possible form compromise under fatigue or intensity.

insights.title: Low session frequency masks moderate per-run load
insights.body: Though only 6 runs this month, average aerobic TE is 2.6 and includes a 3.4 TE long run (11.1 km) and two 3.4 TE efforts — meaning individual sessions are demanding. With just 6 runs vs. 10 last month, recovery opportunities have decreased despite lower total volume.

recommendations.action: Do one 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm, pace ~9:00–9:30 min/km) before June 20, focusing on relaxed arm swing and landing under center of mass.
recommendations.reason: Your Z2 time dropped from 43% to 31%, and average HR rose +8 bpm — this session will restore aerobic stimulus without accumulating fatigue.

recommendations.action: Repeat your 3.0 km fast run (6:33 min/km) but limit vertical oscillation to ≤7.8 cm by shortening stride to ≤88 m and maintaining cadence ≥160 spm — use real-time VO feedback if available.
recommendations.reason: Your fastest run showed elevated VO (8.4 cm) and high GC variability — refining form here protects efficiency gains while preserving speed.

recommendations.action: Add 2 minutes of post-run barefoot drills (A-skips, straight-leg bounds) after your next two runs to reinforce neuromuscular coordination for higher cadence.
recommendations.reason: Cadence increased +6 spm but stride length and VO also rose — targeted drills can help decouple speed from excessive bounce.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish Z2 as the foundation for sustainable speed — using heart rate discipline to rebuild volume tolerance and reinforce efficient movement patterns at sub-threshold intensities.
suggested_sessions: 3.0 km progressive run (start Z2, finish Z3 @ 148–152 bpm)
4.0 km easy run + 2 min barefoot form drills
